transcript.text: bosch washer FD 9409 not draining. ive cleaned the filter already. what part do i need?

I can't name the part with confidence yet. With the filter already cleaned, the drain pump is the most likely part, but a jammed impeller or a kinked or blocked drain hose gives exactly the same symptom and costs nothing to fix. A couple of quick checks will tell us which it is. One note: on Bosch machines the 'FD' number is usually the production date rather than the model. The model (E-Nr, often starting WA or WAN/WAT/WAU) is normally on the label around the door opening or on the inside of the filter flap. You'll want that if you do end up needing a part. Do these with the machine switched off and unplugged, with towels and a shallow tray down because there may be water left inside: 1. Take the filter out again and shine a torch into the opening. Turn the small plastic impeller (the vanes) gently with a finger. If something is caught (a coin, hair grip or underwire), remove it, as that's very often the whole fault. If it turns with a slightly lumpy, magnetic feel, that's normal. If it's stiff, won't move, or the vanes are broken, the pump is the problem.
2. Pull the machine out a little and check the grey drain hose at the back for kinks or crushing. Also check where it goes into the standpipe or under-sink waste. A blocked sink trap or spigot, especially one that's newly fitted, is a common culprit.
3. Refit the filter firmly, plug in and run a drain or spin-only programme. Listen at the bottom front. If you hear a hum or buzz but no water moves, and the steps above were clear, the pump is jammed or failed. If it's completely silent, it's still most likely the pump, though occasionally it's the wiring or control board. If the impeller turns freely, the hose and waste are clear, and it still won't pump, then the drain pump is the likely part. On most Bosch machines it's an owner-replaceable job once you know the exact model. Tell me what you find, especially whether the pump hums or stays silent.

Impeller turns but feels a bit stiff and gritty in places. Hose behind looks OK. When I run it the pump hums loudly with a little rattle but no water moves. The E-Nr on the label is rubbed off, so FD 9409 is all I can read. So is it the pump?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump]
Yes, I'm fairly confident it's the drain pump. A loud hum with a rattle and no water moving fits a worn pump, and so does an impeller that feels stiff and gritty in places. A healthy impeller has a light, slightly notchy magnetic feel but turns smoothly. Grittiness usually means the pump's bearing or magnet chamber is worn or packed with debris, so the motor buzzes but can't spin the impeller properly under load. Before you buy anything, two quick things are worth ruling out. 1. If the hose goes into a sink waste or standpipe, pull it out and run the drain programme into a bucket. If water now pumps out strongly, the blockage is in your plumbing, not the machine.
2. With the machine unplugged and the filter out, shine a torch deep into the opening for sand, grit or a small object lodged behind the impeller. If you find and clear something and the impeller then turns smoothly, test it again before ordering a part. If both are clear, replace the drain pump. On most Bosch machines it's a reasonable DIY job. - Unplug the machine and turn off the water.
• Drain any water left inside into a tray first.
• Expect to remove the bottom front panel, or tip the machine back, to reach the pump. If you're not comfortable with that, an engineer will do it quickly, and it's normally well worth repairing rather than replacing the machine. You'll need the model number to get the right pump, since FD 9409 is only the production code. - The original manual, receipt or guarantee paperwork.
• A second sticker on the back of the machine.
• The label on the old pump itself once it's out. Parts suppliers can often match from that.
• Bosch customer service, who may be able to help if you give them the FD number and any serial number you can read.
